      #
      #  The client also includes its authentication credentials as described
      #  in Section 2.3. of [RFC6749].
      #
      #  The authorization server first validates the client credentials (in
      #  case of a confidential client) and then verifies whether the token
      #  was issued to the client making the revocation request.
      return if server.client

      # If this validation [client credentials / token ownership] fails, the request is
      # refused and the  client is informed of the error by the authorization server as
      # described below.
      #
      # @see 2.2.1.  Error Response
      #
      # The error presentation conforms to the definition in Section 5.2 of [RFC6749].
      render json: revocation_error_response, status: :forbidden
    end

    # OAuth 2.0 Section 2.1 defines two client types, "public" & "confidential".
    #
    # RFC7009
    # Section 5. Security Considerations
    # A malicious client may attempt to guess valid tokens on this endpoint
    # by making revocation requests against potential token strings.
    # According to this specification, a client's request must contain a
    # valid client_id, in the case of a public client, or valid client
    # credentials, in the case of a confidential client. The token being
    # revoked must also belong to the requesting client.
    #
    # Once a confidential client is authenticated, it must be authorized to
    # revoke the provided access or refresh token. This ensures one client
    # cannot revoke another's tokens.
    #
    # Doorkeeper determines the client type implicitly via the presence of the
    # OAuth client associated with a given access or refresh token. Since public
    # clients authenticate the resource owner via "password" or "implicit" grant
    # types, they set the application_id as null (since the claim cannot be
    # verified).
    #
    # https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-2.1
    # https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7009
    def authorized?
      # Token belongs to specific client, so we need to check if
      # authenticated client could access it.
      if token.application_id? && token.application.confidential?
        # We authorize client by checking token's application
        server.client && server.client.application == token.application
      else
        # Token was issued without client, authorization unnecessary
        true
      end
    end

    def revocable_token
      return @revocable_token if defined? @revocable_token

      @revocable_token =
        if params[:token_type_hint] == "refresh_token"
          refresh_token
        else
          access_token || refresh_token
        end
    end

    def refresh_token
      token = Doorkeeper.config.access_token_model.by_refresh_token(params["token"])
      return unless token

      RevocableTokens::RevocableRefreshToken.new(token)
    end

    def access_token
      token = Doorkeeper.config.access_token_model.by_token(params["token"])
      return unless token

      RevocableTokens::RevocableAccessToken.new(token)
    end

    def strategy
      @strategy ||= server.token_request(params[:grant_type])
    end

    def authorize_response
      @authorize_response ||= begin
        before_successful_authorization
        auth = strategy.authorize
        context = build_context(auth: auth)
        after_successful_authorization(context) unless auth.is_a?(Doorkeeper::OAuth::ErrorResponse)
        auth

> # Critique of `specs/07_09_22_31_PAT_tokens_spec.md` (draft v2, 2026-09-07)
> 
> **Round 2.** Round 1 returned C-1 to C-11; all were accepted (D-020) and applied. Per `CLAUDE.md`, a third round would need the human's explicit go-ahead. Findings below continue the numbering at C-12.
> 
> ## Verdict
> 
> **NEEDS WORK**, one blocking finding. It is a factual error that round 1 introduced (my C-4 misread Doorkeeper's revoke endpoint), not a design problem. The fix is text plus removing one test. The C-1 and C-2 resolutions are correct and generate no new defects.
> 
> ## Blocking findings
> 
> **C-12. The `/oauth/revoke` claim is false and its new test cannot pass.**
> - Where: 4.1 third side-effect bullet, 8.3 `test_oauth_revoke_endpoint_should_revoke_pat_without_client`, section 9 README bullet, D-020's record of C-4.
> - Problem: round 1 read only `authorized?` (`doorkeeper/tokens_controller.rb:102-112`). The controller also has `before_action :validate_presence_of_client, only: [:revoke]` (l.5). That filter returns early only when `server.client` is present (l.67), which requires valid `client_id`/`client_secret` of a registered `Doorkeeper::Application`; otherwise it renders `revocation_error_response` with 403 (l.76) and nothing is revoked. So a bare `POST /oauth/revoke` with a PAT is refused. The precise behaviour: with credentials of *any* registered OAuth application, an application-less token passes `authorized?` and is revoked; without them, 403. Also, `revoke` reads `params["token"]` (l.148), not `access_token_methods`, so our configuration change does not touch this endpoint at all.
> - Why it matters: the spec now promises the implementer a green test that will be red, and the README would state something a maintainer can disprove with one curl. My error, and it must not reach the MR.
> - Suggested resolution: rewrite the bullet as "`/oauth/revoke` is unaffected by this slice; it revokes an application-less token only when the caller authenticates as a registered OAuth application, which is Doorkeeper behaviour we do not change". Drop the test from 8.3 (it would pin gem behaviour outside our diff). Remove the "self-revocation" README line in section 9. Because `decisions.md` is append-only, add a short entry correcting D-020's C-4 sentence and citing this finding.
> 
> ## Non-blocking findings
> 
> **C-13. The mechanism D-022 relies on is not in `architecture.md`.**
> - Where: `architecture.md` 1.4 or 1.10; 1.3.1.
> - Problem: the design now depends on `render_flash_messages` printing only String values (`application_helper.rb:516-524`) and on it being the sole flash iterator in `app/` and `lib/` (verified by grep). Neither fact is recorded. The `/oauth/token/info` transport effect (`doorkeeper/rails/helpers.rb:72-76` uses `access_token_methods`; `as_json` tolerates a nil application via `application.try(:uid)`, `access_token_mixin.rb:352`) is also absent from 1.3.1.
> - Suggested resolution: one bullet each.
> 
> **C-14. Rails' development error page dumps the session, including the previous flash.**
> - Where: 5.2 and section 9 limits.
> - Problem: on an exception, `actionpack-7.2.3/.../rescues/_request_and_response.html.erb:8` renders `debug_hash @request.session` behind a "Toggle session dump" link. The session still holds the flash committed by the *previous* request until `commit_flash` runs after the action, so an exception on the redirected GET shows the plaintext there even with the D-022 callback. Only when `consider_all_requests_local` is true, which is development and test only (`config/environments/development.rb:17`); production shows a static page.
> - Suggested resolution: no code. One sentence in the README limits, since reviewers will verify in the development Docker environment.
> 
> **C-15. Spec wording nits from the fixes.**
> - Where: 3.2 italics (spec l.163) still explains `attr_accessor :lifetime_days`; the model now has `attr_reader` plus a writer.
> - Where: 5.2 `read_new_token_from_flash` says "moves ... and deletes". `FlashHash#delete` returns `self` (`flash.rb:189-193`), not the value, so state explicitly "read the value, then delete the key".
> - Where: 10 acceptance. `test:autoload` was dropped in favour of `zeitwerk:check`; CI runs `test:autoload` (`conventions.md`), so keep both. D-020 says "replaces"; the intent was "adds".
> - Where: D-022 text says "a 403 (REST API disabled, sudo mode)". Sudo mode never guards `index` and renders 200 when it intercepts. Record-only; mention in the correcting entry from C-12 if the human wants the log precise.
> 
> ## Challenged decisions
> 
> None. D-020 needs the factual correction in C-12, not a reversal.
> 
> ## What is good
> 
> - **C-1 resolution verified.** `Redmine::SafeAttributes#safe_attributes=` ends in `self.attributes = ...` (`safe_attributes.rb:90`), which dispatches to the `lifetime_days=` writer, so form Strings, test Integers and junk all normalise before the inclusion check; a blank value yields exactly one error (C-6).
> - **C-2 resolution verified.** Controller callbacks run after the six `ApplicationController` ones (`application_controller.rb:64`), all of which only redirect, and before `require_login`, `require_rest_api_enabled`, sudo mode and the action. The Array wrap is skipped by the layout's `is_a?(String)` guard, and that helper is the only flash iterator in the tree. The functional-test plan holds: `ActionController::TestCase` writes `flash.to_session_value` into `@request.session["flash"]` after each request (`test_case.rb:643-646`), so the second `get :index` sees the value.
> - **D-021 is precise** about the Basic-username difference, and the `/oauth/token/info` statement in 4.1 is correct.
> - **Shared documents.** `decisions.md` has only additions since the last commit; `architecture.md` 1.3 (e), 1.6, 1.8 and section 3 now agree with the spec.
> 
> Hand-over: the planner should apply C-12 (text, drop one test, one correcting decision entry) and, if convenient, C-13 to C-15. None of these changes the design, so I recommend the human approve v3 for the implementer without a third critic round.

## D-028: The README reports the pre-existing nil-user bug in `find_current_user` as a minor finding

  users) and then calls `user.oauth_scope=` unconditionally
  (`application_controller.rb:134-138`). A blocked user with a still-valid OAuth token

  the guard in passing inside the "important items" bullet.

  states the mechanism, the trigger (blocked user, valid token), the symptom (500),
  the fix (guard, now 401) and the test, and says it has not been reported upstream
  by us, so maintainers can decide. Spec section 9 amended accordingly.
- Alternatives considered: leaving it inside the "important items" list (too terse
  for a behaviour change in the authentication path); filing an upstream ticket now
  (the human's call, outside the planner's remit).
- Consequences: README content only; no code or test change.

## D-029: The empty token list says there are no tokens, not "No data to display"
- Date: 2026-09-08
- Decided by: human
- Context: After step 6 the human opened `my/api_tokens` with no tokens and saw
  Redmine's generic `label_no_data` ("No data to display"), which the spec (5.3) had
  prescribed. On a page whose purpose is one list, "data" is vague; the message should
  say what is missing and what to do.
- Decision: New key `text_personal_access_token_none` ("You have no personal access
  tokens yet. Create one below to access the REST API."), rendered inside the same
  `<p class="nodata">` so the styling matches other empty states (precedent for custom
  text in `p.nodata`: `app/views/sudo_mode/new.html.erb:2`). `label_no_data` is no
  longer reused by this feature. Spec 5.3, 5.4 and 8.4 amended; one functional test
  added.
- Alternatives considered: keep `label_no_data` (consistent with most Redmine lists,
  but uninformative here); hide the paragraph entirely (the form below then looks
  like the whole page, with no explanation).
- Consequences: one i18n key, one view line, one test in step 6's commit or a small
  follow-up commit at the human's discretion.
- References: spec 5.3, 5.4, 8.4; D-005
